guide.summary: Churches, university museums, libraries and markets in central Bologna, with pasta lunches, trattoria dinners, bakeries and bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan museum days around closures: Palazzo Fava and the university museums on Via Zamboni close on Mondays, and Galleria Modernissimo closes on Tuesdays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Palazzo Fava, Museo di Palazzo Poggi, Museo della Specola and the Orto Botanico close on Mondays (non-holiday Mondays for the university sites), and Santo Stefano suspends tourist visits on Mondays. Galleria Modernissimo is closed on Tuesdays and Ristorante Al Pappagallo closes on Tuesdays.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Museo della Specola admits up to 15 visitors at the start of each hour and strongly recommends booking. Trattoria Da Cesari takes bookings by phone, and Café Marinetti's aperitif must be booked by email.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Osteria dell'Orsa does not accept reservations, and Sfoglia Rina's restaurant on Via Castiglione takes no bookings either. At Osteria del Sole you can bring your own food, and it serves only wine and beer.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Basilica di San Petronio requires shoulders and knees covered, asks you to remove hats, and does not allow suitcases or luggage. Its panoramic terrace is permanently closed.

guide.dek: Base yourself between Piazza Maggiore and Via Zamboni, and check each sight's closing day before you plan museums and dinners.
intro: You can see much of central Bologna on foot from Piazza Maggiore. The Basilica di San Petronio opens daily from 10:00 to 18:00, and its museum is free, while the Chapel of the Magi route costs €5. Dress rules apply: cover your shoulders and knees, and leave suitcases behind. The basilica's panoramic terrace is permanently closed. A short walk away, the Biblioteca dell'Archiginnasio on Piazza Luigi Galvani runs talks and book presentations, though its reading room is temporarily closed.

For views and science, head to Via Zamboni 33. The Museo della Specola lets in up to 15 visitors at the start of each hour, and the terrace stays shut in rain or snow, so book ahead. In the same building, the Museo di Palazzo Poggi shows 'Utagawa Kuniyoshi (1798-1861)' until 20 June 2027. Both close on non-holiday Mondays. The nearby Orto Botanico on Via Irnerio is free, opens 9:00 to 15:00 in winter, and has some areas closed by renovation works.

Exhibitions run well into winter. At Palazzo Fava on Via Manzoni, 'Magnus. Eroi e no' runs from 7 November 2026 to 10 January 2027, with family workshops on Saturdays. Galleria Modernissimo, beneath Piazza Re Enzo, shows 'VIVA VARDA! Il cinema è donna' until 10 January 2027 and closes on Tuesdays. The Basilica di Santo Stefano opens for tourist visits from Tuesday to Sunday. Above the city, the Santuario della Madonna di San Luca opens daily from 7:00 to 18:00.

For food, Trattoria Da Cesari on Via de' Carbonesi serves tagliatelle alla Bolognese and tortellini in brodo and closes on Sundays. Ristorante Diana on Via Volturno closes on Sunday evenings and Mondays. Osteria dell'Orsa and Sfoglia Rina take no reservations, so plan on walking in. For bread and pastries, try Paolo Atti & Figli on Via Caprarie, then have an evening glass at Osteria del Sole, where you can bring your own food.
summaryCards: Start at the Basilica di San Petronio, walk to the Archiginnasio, and finish with tortellini at Trattoria Da Cesari.
Have breakfast at Pasticceria Impero on Via Caprarie, then visit the free Orto Botanico from Tuesday to Sunday.
Book the Museo della Specola and phone Da Cesari ahead, but expect to walk in at Osteria dell'Orsa and Sfoglia Rina.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several sites could not be read: MAMbo and Aroma (certificate errors), Museo Ducati and MAST (HTTP 403), the Museo Civico Archeologico (security check), and the Pinacoteca Nazionale (DNS failure and connection refused). The Two Towers' booking domain redirects to the tourism board, so it was not used. Hours were not published or not readable for Paolo Atti & Figli, Forno Brisa (Via Galliera), Salumeria Simoni, Ristorante I Portici and Café Marinetti, and only the day's hours were shown for the Archiginnasio and Salaborsa. Several restaurants (Tamburini, Osteria dell'Orsa, Diana, Al Pappagallo, Pasticceria Impero) publish hours but no dated 2026 content, so they are rated medium confidence.
